questions.prompt: What does the term 'DTP' stand for?
What is meant by the term 'grey hat hacking'?
questions.markSchemeHint: Hacking into a system without permission (illegally) to find vulnerabilities, usually without malicious intent (e.g., reporting flaws to the owner or asking for a fee to fix them).

questions.prompt: Which one of the following would be used to develop information?
questions.markSchemeHint: C) Information = Data + Context + Structure (1 mark).

questions.prompt: Link each cyber-security term to its relevant impact.
matchingRight: A customer's personal data is illegally accessed and used without their permission.
Customers may be unable to purchase goods/services via a company's website.
Fake bank accounts created using personal details without the individual's knowledge.
Re-directing a user to a fake website.
questions.markSchemeHint: Data Theft -> A customer's personal data is illegally accessed and used without their permission (1); Denial of Service -> Customers may be unable to purchase goods/services via a company's website (1); Identity Theft -> Fake bank accounts created using personal details without the individual's knowledge (1).

questions.figureNote: Fig. 3 on Page 2 shows a hand holding a strong magnet over a 1.0TB hard disk drive.
questions.scenarioContext: Refer to Fig. 3 on Page 2 of the PDF.
questions.prompt: Identify the method being used to destroy data securely from the hard drive.

questions.figureNote: Fig. 4 on Page 3 shows a mobile app prototype with 'Select Date: JUNE 2021' calendar picker, a 'Select Class' drop-down box, and a 'Book Class' button.
questions.scenarioContext: Fig. 4 shows a prototype of a mobile app for Progress Performance (PP) showing how data could be entered by PP customers.
questions.prompt: Identify the data type that is being used by customers in Fig. 4 to select classes. Justify why this data type is a suitable choice for PP.
questions.markSchemeHint: Text / String / Alphanumeric (or Date for the calendar) (1). Justification (2): class names consist of letters/words (or dates use calendar format), presented via a limited-choice drop-down list/date picker which prevents spelling/formatting errors and ensures valid bookings.

questions.figureNote: Fig. 4 on Page 4 shows the Progress Performance mobile app prototype.
questions.scenarioContext: Amir has found some images on a website he wants to use for the prototype.
questions.prompt: Identify the legislation that covers the use of images from a website.
Describe one way that Amir can comply with the legislation you have identified in part (a).
questions.markSchemeHint: Contact the copyright owner to ask for permission (1) and pay any licence fee / acknowledge the creator, OR use royalty-free / Creative Commons / self-created images (1).

questions.scenarioContext: Amir is developing a mobile app for Progress Performance (PP) which offers exercise classes. Amir has told PP of the importance of securely backing up the data gathered from the mobile app.
questions.prompt: Identify and describe two impacts on PP if the data is not backed up.
questions.markSchemeHint: 2 marks each (impact + description): permanent loss of customer/booking records if hardware fails or ransomware hits; financial loss/refunds due to lost payment/class bookings; loss of customer trust and reputation; inability to run classes smoothly / operational downtime; potential fines under Data Protection Act.

questions.scenarioContext: Progress Performance (PP) launched the mobile app with real-time data (RTD) functionality.
questions.prompt: State two benefits to the customer of the mobile app providing information in this way.
questions.markSchemeHint: Any two: sees live/up-to-the-second class availability (avoids double booking or turning up to full classes); instant booking confirmation; immediate alerts for class cancellations or timetable changes.

questions.figureNote: Table 5 on Page 6 shows CUST_ID values: 0051, 0027, 0106, 0056, 0104, 0057.
questions.scenarioContext: Table 5 shows downloaded class booking data with CUST_ID values: 0051, 0027, 0106, 0056, 0104, 0057.
questions.prompt: Identify a suitable data type for CUST_ID.
questions.markSchemeHint: Text / String / Alphanumeric (required to keep the leading zeros such as '0051', which an Integer type would strip).

questions.scenarioContext: Customers of Progress Performance have been advised to use physical security measures when using the app on their mobile device.
questions.prompt: Identify one physical security measure that could be used by customers. Justify your answer.
questions.markSchemeHint: Measure (1): Biometrics (fingerprint/facial recognition), keeping phone locked in a gym locker, privacy screen filter. Justification (2): prevents unauthorised people physically accessing the device/app and viewing personal or payment details.

questions.scenarioContext: As the number of customers using the mobile app has increased, Progress Performance (PP) is considering different data storage solutions to store and access the data downloaded from the mobile app.
questions.prompt:
Discuss the use of a cloud-based storage solution and a physical storage solution for storing and accessing the data downloaded from the mobile app.

In your answer you must consider:
• benefits and drawbacks of a cloud-based storage solution
• benefits and drawbacks of a physical storage solution.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 10-mark Level of Response. Comprehensive, balanced evaluation of cloud storage (scalable for growing customer numbers, remote access for Leo/instructors, automated backups vs ongoing fees, internet dependency, third-party security) vs physical storage (full local control, offline access, one-off purchase vs limited capacity, physical theft/fire damage, manual off-site backups) applied directly to PP, ending with a justified recommendation.

questions.prompt: Select the type of legislation that gives the customer the right to make a subject access request.

questions.figureNote: Fig. 6 on Page 10 shows a mobile touch screen tablet next to the school canteen exit asking students to tap a Happy/Neutral/Sad face, Enter Name, Enter Date of Birth, and press Submit Feedback.
questions.scenarioContext: Westwood Catering (WCA) provides breakfast and lunch for students in a school. It installs a mobile touch screen device next to the canteen exit (Fig. 6) that transmits feedback wirelessly to WCA's information systems.
questions.prompt:
Discuss the advantages of using this data collection method.

In your answer you must consider the needs of:
• the School
• WCA.
questions.markSchemeHint: OCR 8-mark Level of Response. Needs of the School: quick/easy smiley-face feedback doesn't cause queues at canteen exit, paperless/eco-friendly, helps monitor student meal satisfaction and healthy eating. Needs of WCA: wireless real-time transmission to information systems, automatic collation/analysis without manual data entry, identifies popular/unpopular meals quickly to reduce food waste and improve menus.

questions.figureNote: Page 12 shows an email template from the Headteacher to info@westwoodcatering.org (Subject: Data Collection Concerns) referencing Fig. 6 (which asks students for Name and Date of Birth!).
questions.scenarioContext: The Headteacher of a School is concerned about the data being collected on students as shown in Fig. 6 (which asks students to enter their Name and Date of Birth for a canteen food rating).
questions.prompt: Complete the three sections of the Headteacher's email to Westwood Catering (info@westwoodcatering.org).
subFieldLabels: 1. There are concerns over the information you are collecting from the students because: (2 marks)
2. From a legal perspective you can only: (2 marks)
3. A consequence of using the feedback in its current form is: (2 marks)
questions.markSchemeHint: Section 1 (2): collects excessive/unnecessary personal data (student Name and Date of Birth) from minors/children without parental consent or privacy notice. Section 2 (2): under UK GDPR/Data Protection Act 2018, only collect data that is adequate, relevant, and limited to what is necessary (anonymous ratings), with lawful basis/consent and secure storage. Section 3 (2): breach of Data Protection Act/GDPR risking ICO investigation/heavy fines, legal action from parents, and reputational damage/loss of contract.

questions.figureNote: Fig. 7 on Page 13 shows 'Weekly Canteen Feedback' with a pie chart (62% happy, 25% sad, 13% neutral), smiley face icons, knife/fork bullet points, simple language, and 'We promise next week to...' promises.
questions.scenarioContext: The feedback is displayed via a digital screen in the canteen (Fig. 7). Age and accessibility are two demographics that WCA had to consider.
questions.prompt: Describe one way that age has been considered by WCA when displaying the feedback.
questions.markSchemeHint: Uses simple/child-friendly vocabulary and short bullet points (1) plus visual smiley-face icons and a simple pie chart so school-age students can understand it quickly without reading dense text (1).

questions.figureNote: Refer to Fig. 7 on Page 14 (high-contrast black text on white background, large bold headings, percentages alongside smiley icons, clear boxes).
questions.scenarioContext: Refer to Fig. 7 on Page 14 of the PDF.
questions.prompt: Describe one way that accessibility has been considered by WCA when displaying the feedback.
questions.markSchemeHint: High contrast dark text on a plain white background / clean sans-serif font / large headings / both icons and percentage numbers so colour-blind or visually impaired students can read the display easily (2 marks).

questions.figureNote: Refer to Fig. 7 on Page 14. The School would like to share the Weekly Canteen Feedback with the parents of the students.
questions.scenarioContext: The School would like to share the canteen feedback from the survey (Fig. 7) with the parents of the students.
questions.prompt: Identify one distribution channel that could be used to share the feedback from the survey with the parents of the students. Justify your answer.
questions.markSchemeHint: Channel (1): Email / School Website / School App / Social Media / Messaging (SMS/parent portal). Justification (2): explains why it effectively reaches parents (e.g., email/parent app sends directly to parents' devices quickly at no printing cost; school website allows 24/7 access alongside menus).
